name: Isotretinoin
summary: The high-impact acne drug for severe or refractory disease, powerful enough that its adverse-effect and monitoring logic must be taken seriously.
good: Severe acne, scarring risk, or refractory disease where disease modification matters.
bad: Pregnancy risk without strict prevention and monitoring discipline.
clinicalPearls: It is one of the few drugs that can change the long-term course of acne rather than just suppressing it temporarily.
mechanism: Normalizes follicular keratinization, reduces sebum, and reshapes the acne microenvironment.
indications: Severe nodulocystic acne, scarring acne, and acne that has not responded adequately to standard therapy.
interactionNotes: Avoid tetracyclines because of intracranial-hypertension risk; vitamin A supplementation is also a problem.

warnings: Teratogenicity, dryness, lipid changes, liver enzyme elevation, and possible mood discussion are central issues.

originalFields: Mechanism
Normalizes follicular keratinization, reduces sebum, and reshapes the acne microenvironment.
Typical uses
Severe nodulocystic acne, scarring acne, and acne that has not responded adequately to standard therapy.
Key cautions
Teratogenicity, dryness, lipid changes, liver enzyme elevation, and possible mood discussion are central issues.
Important interactions
Avoid tetracyclines because of intracranial-hypertension risk; vitamin A supplementation is also a problem.
Pearl
It is one of the few drugs that can change the long-term course of acne rather than just suppressing it temporarily.
Best use case
Severe nodulocystic acne, treatment-resistant moderate acne, or acne causing significant scarring — typically after other options have been tried.
Speed of response
Slower than topicals at first, but uniquely offers long-term or potentially permanent remission after one completed course — unlike every other agent here, which needs ongoing use.
Irritation risk
Not topical irritation — near-universal systemic dryness of skin, lips, and eyes, dose-related.
Pigmentation relevance
Can help prevent future PIH by preventing the inflammatory nodules that cause it, but does not treat existing pigmentation.
Barrier effects
Significant, near-universal systemic drying — daily heavy moisturizer and lip care become routine during treatment.
Wash-off vs leave-on
Not applicable — oral medication, taken with a fat-containing meal to improve absorption.
AM / PM use
Per prescriber; taken with food regardless of time of day.
Combination compatibility

Contraindicated with tetracycline-class antibiotics (additive intracranial hypertension risk) and additional vitamin A; requires a strict, monitored pregnancy-prevention program given severe teratogenicity.
